scope: Supplementary actual SQLite interruption audit against evolving source; not a full worker or engine power-loss test
environment: Local isolated Linux Docker, read-only source/root, network none, synthetic private state in tmpfs
procedure: Explicitly bootstrap fresh v2; child SQLite connection begins an uncommitted transaction with cache_size=1 and FULL synchronous, inserts 1000 normalized synthetic object rows to force pager spill, signals transaction-open; terminate that exact owned child; invoke normal read-only startup guard
interpretation: Current guard intentionally refuses a journal requiring SQLite recovery. Logical exception/reopen tests and coordinator disconnect tests do not prove automatic restart after an interrupted pager transaction. No recovery or marker repair was attempted by this audit.
remaining: Design and qualify bounded same-owner/profile hot-journal recovery before claiming automatic worker power-loss recovery. Retain strict ownership, original ABI, root/inode, sidecar bounds, quota and no-foreign-adoption checks. This is separate from the current indexed transfer optimization.
cleanup: Only this owned disposable synthetic temporary directory and child were closed by the test fixture; no installed state, image, volume, NAS or original files changed
